title: Power Automate: Delinea Secret Server as a credential provider for desktop flows
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing credential controls, licensing and published flow-run rates are supported. It distinguishes the planned Delinea provider from existing CyberArk and Azure Key Vault functionality and leaves undocumented provider-specific requirements open.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support Delinea Secret Server as an external credential provider for desktop flows.
claims.quote: Power Automate will support Delinea Secret Server as an external credential provider for desktop flows.

claims.claim: The planned provider lets organisations use credentials managed in Delinea for machine sign-in.
claims.quote: Organizations can securely use credentials managed in Delinea for machine sign-in and credential retrieval during attended and unattended automation.

claims.claim: The planned provider supports retrieving credentials managed in Delinea.
claims.quote: Organizations can securely use credentials managed in Delinea for machine sign-in and credential retrieval during attended and unattended automation.

claims.claim: Existing CyberArk credentials retrieve CCP CyberArk secrets from the vault at runtime.
claims.quote: This feature enables you to create a Power Automate credential that retrieves CCP CyberArk secrets from the vault during runtime.

claims.claim: An Azure Key Vault credential used in a desktop flow connection signs into the machine at runtime for attended and unattended runs.
claims.quote: Used in a desktop flow connection, the credential is used to sign into the machine during runtime (attended and unattended runs).

claims.claim: The Get credential variable for existing CyberArk credentials is marked sensitive.
claims.quote: Define the name of your produced variable. This variable is marked as sensitive and can't be modified.

claims.claim: The Get credential variable for existing Azure Key Vault credentials is marked sensitive.
claims.quote: Define the name of the variable you create. This variable is marked as "sensitive" and can't be changed.

claims.claim: The CyberArk credential guide describes the sensitive variable's value as not stored in logs, subject to the separately stated security-update caveat.
claims.quote: This restriction means the value of this variable isn't stored in the logs.

claims.claim: The Azure Key Vault credential guide describes the sensitive variable's value as not stored in logs, subject to the separately stated security-update caveat.
claims.quote: This means the value of this variable isn't stored in the logs.

claims.claim: Unpatched Power Automate for desktop versions 2.62 through 2.66 are affected by the sensitive-value log exposure vulnerability.
claims.quote: A potential vulnerability (CVE-2026-40374) that can expose sensitive values in flow execution logs affects Power Automate for desktop versions 2.62 through 2.66.

claims.claim: The sensitive-variable vulnerability affects global sensitive variables used in local subflows.
claims.quote: The issue affects only flows that use global sensitive variables in local subflows.

claims.claim: Installing a listed patched build or release 2.67.143.26090 or later fixes the sensitive-variable vulnerability.
claims.quote: If you need an update for an earlier release, get one of the following downloads: ... Release 2.67.143.26090 and all later versions include this security fix.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop flows do not require human supervision.
claims.quote: Unattended desktop flows are ideal for automating tasks that don't need human supervision.

claims.claim: The CyberArk certificate is opened and encrypted using the machine group's public key so only registered machines can read it.
claims.quote: The password isn't stored. The certificate is opened and encrypted by using the public key of the machine group so it's only readable from the registered machines.

claims.claim: Power Automate for desktop runs with the same user rights as the user who starts it.
claims.quote: Power Automate for desktop runs with the same user rights as the user who starts it.

claims.claim: Machine sign-in uses the account credentials provided through the desktop flow connection.
claims.quote: Power Automate creates a new session for each unattended run on the machine using the credentials provided in the connection. The flow runs on this session, and then Power Automate signs it off.

claims.claim: General Power Automate desktop-flow security controls apply to desktop flows, without a claim of a Delinea-specific implementation.
claims.quote: This article explains best practices and actionable steps to secure your data: setting up credentials, managing sensitive variables, controlling access to desktop flows and related components, enforcing data loss prevention (DLP) policies, and capturing audit logs.

claims.claim: Sharing an Azure Key Vault credential also shares all environment variables used in the credential.
claims.quote: By sharing your credential, all the environment variables used in the credential are shared as well.

claims.claim: Removing permissions on an Azure Key Vault credential does not remove permissions on its environment variables.
claims.quote: Removing permissions on a credential doesn't remove permissions on the environment variables.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model names Power Automate Premium as including retrieval and use of desktop-flow credentials, while leaving Delinea-specific licensing open.
claims.quote: This article lists the premium robotic process automation (RPA) features and benefits that the Power Automate Premium user license includes ... Credentials | Retrieve and use credentials in desktop flows.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: For unattended desktop-flow executions, Microsoft names Power Automate Process or pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote: For additional capacity, running desktop flows unattended, or licensing flows on their own without use licenses, subscribe to Power Automate Process licenses or enable pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Desktop-flow users in a pay-as-you-go-enabled environment have access to most premium RPA features within that environment.
claims.quote: Desktop flow users in a pay-as-you-go-enabled environment have access to most of the premium features listed earlier in the scope of that specific environment.

claims.claim: The Power Automate flow-run meters covering desktop flows are in preview.
claims.quote: Power Automate flow runs (preview) | Flow runs for premium cloud flows and desktop flows.

claims.claim: Attended desktop runs in a pay-as-you-go environment are priced at $0.60 per run unless the running user's licence includes attended RPA.
claims.quote: Attended runs follow the entitlements of the user running the flow. A user whose license includes attended RPA isn't charged; a user whose license doesn't include it is charged $0.60 per run.

claims.claim: Unattended desktop runs in a pay-as-you-go environment are priced at $3.00 per run regardless of assigned environment capacity.
claims.quote: Unattended runs are charged at $3.00 per run regardless of any capacity assigned to the environment.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The documented pay-as-you-go flow-run consumption is billed to the linked Azure subscription, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: When you choose to use pay-as-you-go, Azure meters bill your Azure subscription for your usage of Power Platform services.

claims.claim: The existing CyberArk credential feature is currently unavailable for US Government Clouds.

claims.claim: Power Automate > Machines > machine or group > Machine details > Configure CyberArk > New application reaches CyberArk application configuration.
claims.quote: From the left navigation, select Machines, and then select the machine or the group. ... In the Machine details, select Configure CyberArk. ... Select New application.

claims.claim: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/flowcredentialapplications creates a CyberArk application record, rather than specifying a Delinea setup contract.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/flowcredentialapplications ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE ... applicationid: Unique ID of the application as registered in the CyberArk CCP

claims.claim: applicationid identifies the application registered in CyberArk CCP.
claims.quote: applicationid | Edm.String | Unique ID of the application as registered in the CyberArk CCP

claims.claim: flowmachinegroupid identifies the application record's machine group.
claims.quote: _flowmachinegroupid_value | flowmachinegroupid | The flow machine group.

claims.claim: primarycertificatefile carries the SSL client certificate for contacting CCP and is encrypted with the group's public key.
claims.quote: primarycertificatefile | Edm.String | Certificate that will be used as an SSL client certificate to contact the CCP. This field is encrypted with the group public key.

claims.claim: Power Automate > Credentials > credential > Share > Add people > role reaches credential sharing permissions.
claims.quote: go to Credentials. ... Select your credential from the list of credentials. ... On the command bar, select Share. ... Select Add people, enter the name of the person ... and then select the role you want to grant to this user

claims.claim: POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/GrantAccess grants record access using PrincipalAccess, and can be used with Credential records.
claims.quote: Grants a security principal (user, team, or organization) access to the specified record. ... PrincipalAccess ... The team or user that is granted access to the specified record.

claims.claim: Access to Credential records referenced by Get credential can be managed through the component page or a Dataverse security role.
claims.quote: Manage access through the dedicated page of each component in the Power Automate portal or through a Dataverse security role that grants access to the records in the component's table. ... Credentials | Use the Get credential action | Share a credential | Credential

claims.claim: PrincipalAccess identifies the security principal and its access rights.
claims.quote: AccessMask ... The access rights of the security principal (user, team, or organization). ... Principal ... The security principal (user, team, or organization).

claims.claim: A CyberArk application cannot currently be associated with machines or groups shared with other users.
claims.quote: You can't currently associate a CyberArk application with machines or groups that you share with other users.

claims.claim: CyberArk application information and its certificate can be configured for a machine or machine group in the Power Automate portal.
claims.quote: To run a desktop flow on a machine or a group by using CyberArk credentials, add your CyberArk application information in the Power Automate portal. ... Select the certificate, which stores the private and the public key of the certificate.

claims.claim: The Dataverse credential table supports create, read, update and delete operations.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/credentials ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE

claims.claim: The Dataverse credential table also documents access operations.
claims.quote: The following operations can be used with the credential entity type. ... GrantAccess | Not Bound ... ModifyAccess | Not Bound ... RetrievePrincipalAccess | Not Bound ... RevokeAccess | Not Bound
